record.title: Open problem: Absence of bi-infinite geodesics in planar iid FPP
record.body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For nondegenerate continuous iid planar passage-time laws in the usual positive-speed regime, determine whether a bi-infinite geodesic exists. Source: Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation, Question31, PDF p.98.
Posed in Auffinger, Damron and Hanson: 50 years of first-passage percolation
Status as recorded in the campaign ledger on 2026-09-07

record.title: Attempt on Absence of bi-infinite geodesics in planar iid FPP
record.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Absence of bi-infinite geodesics in planar iid FPP structural argument Result: Taking geodesics between-ne1 and ne1 gives candidate long paths, but a compactness argument produces a bi-infinite limit through a bounded region only if their distance from that region is tight along a subsequence. Paths can escape every fixed ball while connecting endpoints on opposite sides. Check: An explicit lattice path from(-n,0) up to(-n,n), across to(n,n), then down to(n,0) avoids every fixed ball for all large n; it illustrates the missing compactness anchor, without being asserted to be a geodesic. Obstruction: Finite-geodesic existence does not give the required anchoring. Proving or ruling out such anchoring under iid passage weights remains unresolved here.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0117-absence-of-bi-infinite-geodesics-in-planar-iid-fpp
No independent review
